headline: Route turns with Brisk-S and the few-shot prompt: it is the only one of the {n_candidates} configurations inside all three gates, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few} a month.
lede: It reaches {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean} balanced accuracy, its whole interval above the gate, and holds every cell floor. What could change the call is latency: its p95 of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95} has no interval, so a production measurement above {criteria.p95.threshold} would leave no configuration standing.

caveats.material_if: only if Brisk-S few-shot's true p95 is more than {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} slower than measured: then it misses the budget and no configuration passes every gate.

only if a fresh run reads Brisk-S few-shot's balanced accuracy more than {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap} points lower, or its Complex × News cell more than {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap} points lower; as the one passer of {n_candidates}, its figures read somewhat high.
only for claims that one configuration beats another; the call reads each configuration against fixed gates, not against a control.

decision.text: Ship Brisk-S with the few-shot prompt on all turns. It clears overall balanced accuracy at {overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.interval}, every one of the nine cell floors, and the latency budget at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95}.

Every Atlas-M prompt and Brisk-S with the rubric prompt miss the latency budget (Brisk-S rubric at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.rubric.p95}). Nano-XS few-shot clears latency and, on its point estimate, overall accuracy, but misses the Complex × News cell at {cells.complex.news.nano-xs.few.accuracy.mean}, clear below the floor. The zero-shot prompts and Nano-XS rubric miss accuracy.

The thinnest margin is overall accuracy: {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap} points above the gate, interval {overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.interval}, and above {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value} nothing passes. Complex × News is {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap} points above its floor; in noise the two are about equally safe, each more than twice its half-width. Latency headroom of {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} rests on a point estimate.
Measure Brisk-S few-shot's p95 latency with an interval under production load; it is the one gate the call cannot yet show it clears beyond noise.

claims.text: Two configurations clear both the latency budget and the overall accuracy gate, Brisk-S and Nano-XS with the few-shot prompt; every Atlas-M prompt and the Brisk-S rubric fall out on latency, the rest on accuracy.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy against p95 latency (log axis), with the gates at {criteria.overall.threshold} and {criteria.p95.threshold}; Nano-XS few-shot's overall interval, {overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.nano-xs.few.interval}, straddles its gate.

claims.text: The cell floor separates the two: at Complex × News, the weakest cell for both, Brisk-S few-shot clears the floor by {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap} points, while Nano-XS few-shot fails there and nowhere else.

evidence.caption: Accuracy in each complexity × domain cell, with its interval and count; the floor is {criteria.cell_floor.threshold}.

claims.text: On Brisk-S, few-shot examples lift balanced accuracy by {lever.prompt.brisk-s.zero.brisk-s.few.balanced_accuracy.effect} points and the rubric prompt adds only {lever.prompt.brisk-s.few.brisk-s.rubric.balanced_accuracy.effect} more while breaking the latency budget; the prompt's effect depends on the model, and the rubric costs Nano-XS accuracy against few-shot.

evidence.caption: Each model × prompt tile: balanced accuracy, cost per 1,000 turns, p95 latency and whether it passes every gate. Few-shot gains more on Nano-XS than on Atlas-M by {lever.prompt.atlas-m.zero.atlas-m.few.balanced_accuracy.vs.nano-xs.zero.nano-xs.few.difference} points.

explore.outcome: Below Nano-XS few-shot's Complex × News accuracy of {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, Nano-XS few-shot becomes the pick; above Brisk-S few-shot's {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.value}, nothing passes.
The call holds for any gate up to {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value}; above it, nothing passes.
The call holds for any budget at or above {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.value}; below it, nothing passes.

omitted.why: Neither is gated, and both rank the configurations as balanced accuracy does; they don't change the call.

omitted.what: Confusion tables on complexity and domain
omitted.why: Each axis on its own reads well for both few-shot configurations; they don't locate the Complex × News loss, which is a joint error.

omitted.what: The full lever and interaction table
omitted.why: Prompt and model interact clearly (c3 cites the largest interaction), but the call rests on gates read per configuration, not on averaged effects; the full table stays in the appendix.
It is out on latency by a wide margin, so its accuracy doesn't bear on the call.
No failed turns were kept for review in this campaign.

next.text: Measure Brisk-S few-shot's p95 latency, with an interval, under production load.
next.settles: Whether the pick clears the latency budget beyond noise; if not, no configuration passes and the budget or the model needs a decision.

next.text: Add Complex × News examples to the Nano-XS few-shot prompt and re-run that cell and the overall set.
next.settles: Whether Nano-XS few-shot becomes eligible; the monthly cost gap to Brisk-S few-shot is {price.nano-xs.few.brisk-s.few.balanced_accuracy.monthly_cost_gap}. Nano-XS must also clear the overall gate on its interval, today {overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.nano-xs.few.interval}.

next.text: Run Brisk-S few-shot on a fresh holdout of about {settle.criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.overall.cases_needed_two_sided_80} turns, the size at which four runs in five confirm the overall clearance if today's figure is the truth.
next.settles: Whether the pick's thin overall clearance survives outside the set it was chosen on.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases} labelled turns per configuration, each run once, spread over nine complexity × domain cells.
The share of a cell's turns given the correct label, with an interval per cell at the level the cells state, uncorrected.
The plain mean of the nine cell accuracies; its interval is derived from the cells' intervals, read as independent.

Balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold}, each cell at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold}, p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}; all three declared before the run, each read on the point estimate.
p95 only, with no interval stated.
Dollars per million turns, priced at {meta.volume_per_month} turns a month.
No control; prompt and model effects compare two configurations' own intervals as if independent, so they read wide.
